input: Learn the basics of video editing on my laptop

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing which specific skills count as 'basics' for this user determines what to include — cutting clips, transitions, colour correction, audio, titles, exporting, etc. The scope changes the entire learning path.
Understanding who the videos are for (personal memories, a YouTube channel, client work, school projects) shapes which techniques and outputs matter most.
The operating system (Windows or macOS) determines which software is natively available and what tutorials are relevant.
How much time the user can dedicate per week and by when they want to be competent directly affects the pacing and depth of the learning plan.
Whether the user is open to paid software (Premiere Pro, Final Cut) or needs free tools (DaVinci Resolve, CapCut, iMovie) affects every specific recommendation.
Preferred learning style — watching video tutorials, reading guides, hands-on trial-and-error, or a structured course — determines what resources to point them to.
Knowing what a finished, 'good enough' result looks like (e.g., a polished 2-minute YouTube video, a clean family highlight reel) defines when learning is actually complete.

gold.taskTitle: Learn basic video editing on my laptop
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to get started with video editing on their laptop, learning foundational skills from scratch or near-scratch.

questions.title: Which specific editing skills do you want to learn first?
questions.description: For example: cutting and trimming clips, adding transitions, syncing audio, colour correction, adding titles, or exporting. Knowing this defines the exact scope of 'basics' for you.

questions.title: What kind of videos do you plan to make?
questions.description: For example: personal vlogs, YouTube content, school projects, travel memories, or client work. The purpose shapes which techniques and styles are worth prioritising.

questions.title: Does your laptop run Windows or macOS?
questions.description: The operating system determines which software is available by default and which tutorials will be directly applicable to your setup.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to learning?
questions.description: This shapes the pacing of the plan — whether you can go deep in a week or need a gradual multi-week schedule to fit around other commitments.

questions.title: Are you open to paid software, or do you need free tools?
questions.description: This determines whether to recommend free options like DaVinci Resolve or iMovie versus paid tools like Adobe Premiere Pro or Final Cut Pro.

questions.title: How do you learn best — videos, articles, or hands-on practice?
questions.description: Your preferred learning style determines whether to point you to YouTube tutorials, written guides, structured online courses, or practice-first challenges.

questions.title: What would a successful first finished video look like to you?
questions.description: Defining a concrete end goal — like a 2-minute polished clip ready to share — gives the plan a clear finish line and shows when 'basics' have truly been mastered.
